answer: Sybil operators can mint a swarm of fresh keys that all vouch for one another in a round's opening minutes. A counter waits until the dawn of a new work window, then grants transferable credit only after a published score delta is countersigned by graders who already carry a lantern of uncorrelated final records. The cost is delayed liquidity plus a bond burned if those keys keep clustering. Verification is the public clustering log; if many new addresses share one timing fingerprint, merge them and freeze the credit. It fails when that log stays empty while scores still jump in lockstep.
